name: CX
comment: TextMate grammar for CX. Covers the program surface (the code.md §4.1 directive registry — modify / match / for / for-array / for-map / let / fn / def / lib / const / if / pipe / map / reduce / iterator stdlib / resilience / services / concurrency / async / with-* family) plus CXPath value expressions (grammar.ebnf [130]-[135]: '//'-prefix paths, axis specifiers, attribute tests, general predicates), reserved bindings `$_` / `$_position` / `$_last` (code.md §5.5.2), the `(bind $name)` path-step annotation (grammar.ebnf [160a]), bare `pure` / `impure` def modifiers (code.md §12.2), and the universal CX data surface (anchors / IDs / merges / `[table …]` typed tables / glued `::T` annotations / mixed content / [; block comments ] (asymmetric, closes on the matching ]), [# raw text #]). Directive arms and actions are bracket clause-children per code.md §§7-8 ([case …] / [when …] / [else …] / [set …] / [yield …] …) — the v0.7 colon-slot surface (`:case`, `:set`, `:scope`, …) is retired and intentionally unrecognized, as are the `+name`/`-name` bool sigils and `[?try]`. <!-- version-literal-ok -->

embedded.comment: Embedded-language injection — VS Code parity with the tree-sitter queries/injections.scm. The language signal is the wrapping element name ([python [| … |]]) or an explicit lang= attribute ([code lang=bash [# … #]]); the content regions are the [| … |] block body and [# … #] raw text. Each begin consumes the wrapper-open through the content-open delimiter and each end consumes the content-close PLUS the wrapper's closing ], so bracket balance is preserved and the cx structural grammar keeps parsing the surrounding document. lang= patterns precede element-name patterns so an explicit lang= wins, mirroring injections.scm. A language with no installed grammar injects nothing (VS Code drops the rule) and the wrapper falls back to plain cx structure — silently, matching injections.scm.

patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.cx
patterns.comment: Line comment (lexicon [L2]). Anchored to start-of-line or a preceding whitespace so a glued mid-token `#` (`foo#bar` — plain text) and the head-position `#id` declaration (consumed by the #element head match) are not swallowed.

comment-bracket-balance.comment: Inside a [; … ] block comment, consume balanced [ … ] so an inner ] does NOT close the comment early — it closes on the ] matching the [;'s [ (the parser's read_until_close balances bracket depth). The nested region carries no name, so it inherits comment.block.cx and the whole block stays commented.

cx-directive.comment: [?cx …] document processing instruction. Option vocabulary per code.md §13 (include), schema.md (schema / schema-* / frag), ast.md evaluator options (output-target / output-strict / cx-version / allow-eval), formatting.md (format), canonical.md (version).
cx-directive.name: meta.cx-directive.cx

modify-directive.comment: [?modify doc //focus ACTION+] — code.md §8.10 pure-functional update. The 11 actions are bracket clause-children (grammar.ebnf [142]-[148e]); each action head colors as keyword.control.modify via #modify-action-clause.
modify-directive.name: meta.modify-directive.cx

modify-action-clause.comment: One [ACTION …] clause-child inside [?modify] (grammar.ebnf [142]). Longest names first so `set-attr` / `delete-attr` are not tokenised as `set` / `delete`.
modify-action-clause.name: meta.modify-action.cx

match-directive.comment: [?match] — code.md §8.2 pattern dispatch. Arms are bracket clause-children (grammar.ebnf [137]-[140]): [case PATTERN [where GUARD]? BODY] / [when GUARD BODY] / [else BODY]; the single-arm form uses a trailing [yield E] clause (grammar.ebnf [136]).
match-directive.name: meta.match-directive.cx

match-arm-clause.comment: One arm / guard / yield clause-child inside [?match] (grammar.ebnf [136]-[140]). `[where G]` appears nested inside [case …]; `[yield E]` closes the single-arm form.
match-arm-clause.name: meta.match-arm.cx

eval-directive.comment: Directive registry per code.md §4.1 / grammar.ebnf [127e]. [?match] + [?modify] are picked off above by their own repository entries so arm/action clause coloring wins. [?try] is retired (code.md §9.3) and intentionally absent. Includes the dynamic-construction family (code.md §6.4.2-4): element / attr / entry / name / quote / unquote / splice / eval, plus the [?meta] inert annotation (code.md §4.2). Longest names first so `for-array` / `await-all` are not tokenised as `for` / `await`.
eval-directive.name: meta.eval-directive.cx

patterns.name: keyword.other.modifier.cx
patterns.comment: Bare modifier barewords: pure / impure on [?def] (code.md §12.2), lazy on [?const] (§12.3), in-memory on [?lib] (§12.1), asc / desc on [order-by] (§7).

clause-child.comment: Generic [head …] clause-child inside a directive body. Heads per the per-directive registries in code.md §4.1: [?for] clauses (§7 — in / where / yield / yield-array / yield-map / order-by / group-by / limit / take / drop / takewhile / dropwhile / par / stream / ordered / fail-fast), [?if] branches (§8.4 — then / else), [?def] type clauses (§12.2 — returns / throws), [?lib] selective refer (§12.1 — only), [?pipe] taps (§8.9 — tap), [?with-error-hook] clauses (§9.6 — observe / enrich / report / format / sink), [?with-caps] denies (security.md §3 — deny). Longest names first so e.g. `yield-map` is not tokenised as `yield`.
clause-child.name: meta.clause-child.cx

operator-form.comment: Reserved prefix operator heads (grammar.ebnf [125f]/[125g], code.md §6.5) — `[= …]` `[!= …]` `[<= …]` `[+ …]` `[~ …]` and bare and / or / not / cast / union / intersect / except. These are the ONLY spellings of the comparison/boolean/set operators: the former infix forms (`@a=v`, `a != b`, `P and Q`, `A || B`, `instance of`, `cast as`) are parse errors everywhere (grammar.ebnf [132]-[134] retirement note) and are deliberately NOT scoped.
operator-form.name: meta.operator-form.cx

module-call.comment: Qualified module reference `$prefix:local` (code.md §12.1.1 — `[$math:abs -3]`). Matched before the generic `$name` binding so the qualified form colors as a function reference.
module-call.name: entity.name.function.module.cx

type-annotation.comment: Glued `::T` type annotation (grammar.ebnf [26]) — element heads (`[port::u16 8080]`), attributes (`port::u16=8080`), table columns (`name::int`), def params (`$x::int`), typed-bind patterns (`$x::int`, code.md §5.2 rule 14); `::T[]` typed array; `::[]` inferred array. A single-colon `:name` is an atom literal (#scalar), never a type.
type-annotation.name: support.type.cx

path-expr.comment: CXPath expression (grammar.ebnf [130]-[135], [159]-[160a]). Matches '//' and '/'-prefix paths plus axis specifiers, attribute tests, the path-step wildcard `*`, and the `(bind $name)` step annotation. Token-level patterns; the full path grammar lives in libcx — these patterns provide coloring inside directive expression slots. The single '/' step separator is matched ONLY when preceded by ']', a name char, or a sigil-closing char to avoid catching '/' inside string literals (strings are handled by #quoted-string which is included BEFORE #path-expr in directive bodies).

patterns.name: keyword.operator.path.step.cx
patterns.comment: Single '/' step separator. Bound between an identifier/closer ']' on the left and an identifier or '@' or '*' or axis-prefix on the right — biases away from arithmetic and from '/' inside text. Strings are tokenized first by the parent rule, so '/' inside a string literal is never seen here.

patterns.name: keyword.other.bind.cx
patterns.comment: (bind $name) parenthesised peer-annotation on a path Step (grammar.ebnf [160a], code.md §5.5.2). Captured as a single unit so editors can hover-highlight the binding declaration.

patterns.name: keyword.operator.path.wildcard.cx
patterns.comment: Path-step wildcard '*' — matches any element name. Distinct from arithmetic '*' (which appears between two numeric values, not in step position).

reserved-sigils.comment: Reserved bindings in PredicateExpr scope (grammar.ebnf [159], code.md §5.5.2). $_ is the context item; $_position and $_last are 1-based int implicit bindings. These take precedence over the generic `\$[A-Za-z_]...` variable-binding pattern by appearing earlier in directive-body patterns. Outside a predicate body `$_` is also legal as an ordinary binding (e.g. `[?for [in $_ seq] …]`); the highlighter doesn't gate on predicate-scope, but the distinct color makes the sigil-family visible regardless.

patterns.name: variable.language.context-item.cx
patterns.comment: $_ — context-item binding inside PredicateExpr (code.md §5.5.2). Must not match $_position / $_last (handled above), $_foo (user binding starting with _).

interpolation.comment: [?= …] value interpolation (grammar.ebnf [58]) — body is an opaque CXPath expression parsed by the program evaluator.
interpolation.name: meta.interpolation.cx

patterns.comment: Element head, with the optional head-position `#id` declaration glued to it. ID scope is head-position ONLY: the parser lexes a whitespace-preceded `#` ANYWHERE ELSE as a line comment (lexicon [L2]) — `[user [name Alice] #u1 x]` swallows `#u1 x…` to end of line — so a body-position `#name` must color as the comment it is (#comment below), never as an ID.

Unquoted attribute value (bareword/URL/path/dotted): scoped distinctly from the attribute name. Lookbehind `=` keeps it to value position; placed AFTER #scalar so numbers/booleans/dates/atoms keep their own colors.
patterns.name: string.unquoted.cx

scalar.comment: Scalar literals per lexicon.ebnf §3/§4/§6, longest-token-first (datetime before date before numbers) so `2024-01-15` is ONE date token, not int 2024. Numbers ([L20]): optional leading +/- sign, `_` digit separators, hex `0x…`, floats with leading/trailing dot (`.5` / `1.`) and bare exponent (`1e5`); NO leading-zero integers (`042` is Text) and NO 0o/0b (they never existed — both verified Text against the live binary). Durations ([L27]: ns/us/ms/s/m/h/d/w terms) and periods ([L28]: mo/y) are distinct literal types. Datetime ([L24]): fractional seconds and the zone are OPTIONAL, `Z` is uppercase-only, an offset requires the colon.

patterns.name: invalid.illegal.atom.reserved.cx
patterns.comment: `:true` / `:false` / `:null` are FORBIDDEN in atom position (lexicon [L40]) — CXER0100 at lex time; scoped illegal so the rejection is visually obvious.

patterns.name: constant.other.atom.cx
patterns.comment: Atom literal `:NAME` with dotted segments and the terminal `.*` prefix-glob (lexicon [L40], bus.md §2.2) — `:ok`, `:order.placed`, `:order.*` (all verified live). Single colon; the glued double-colon `::T` is a type annotation (#type-annotation).

quoted-string.comment: String literals per lexicon.ebnf §5. Triple-quoted forms FIRST (longest delimiter wins): raw `r'''…'''` / `r"""…"""` ([L31a] — verbatim, no dedent; the `r` is a raw prefix only when glued to the triple), then `'''…'''` / `"""…"""` ([L31] — verbatim multiline, dedented; NO escape processing, so no escape captures inside), then the single-line quoted forms ([L30]) with the closed escape set ([L32]).
